header.title: Open Geotechniek Studio
header.heroAlt: Open Geotechniek Studio: cone test with cone resistance, sleeve friction and friction ratio, with the soil layering on the left
header.label: Geotechnics
header.tagline: From BRO cone test to site drawing and report, in one free app
header.desc: Open a GEF or BRO file, or find every cone test around your site on the map. View qc, fs and Rf with an indicative soil layering, place the points on a site drawing and turn it into a report.

meta.description: Free, open-source app for cone penetration tests (GEF, BRO-xml) and boreholes: charts and soil layering, BRO data on the map, site drawings and PDF reports. For Windows, macOS, Linux and the browser.
meta.title: Open Geotechniek Studio — OpenAEC Foundation

cpt.alt: Cone test with the soil build-up per layer on the left and the normalized Qt/Fr/Bq/Ic analysis on the right
cpt.title: Read a cone test at a glance
cpt.desc: Cone resistance, sleeve friction and friction ratio side by side on one depth axis in NAP. The app divides the test into indicative layers; you adjust the layer boundaries yourself and see a normalized Qt/Fr/Bq/Ic analysis per point.

map.alt: Map with aerial photo, cadastral boundaries and the BRO cone tests in the area as red triangles
map.title: All BRO data around your site
map.desc: Search by address or RD coordinate and load the cone tests, boreholes and groundwater wells from the Dutch subsurface register (BRO) in the visible area. Add aerial photos from 2016 onward, the AHN elevation map, cadastral boundaries or BAG buildings underneath.

drawing.alt: A3 site drawing at 1:500 with cone tests on the map and the OpenAEC title block
drawing.title: A site drawing without a CAD program
drawing.desc: Place cone tests, boreholes or a whole grid of tests on the map, with dimension lines, RD coordinates and notes. Put a PDF or image underneath and export to PDF on A2 or A3, with a completed title block.

report.alt: Report preview with a cone test chart to scale, and on the left the sections to switch on or off
report.title: A report for the project file
report.desc: Choose what goes in: cover, coordinate table, overview map, a page per cone test, the legend and the metadata. Set the chart scale, for example 1:50 across several sheets.

features.label: Features
features.heading: Everything for cone tests and boreholes, in one app
features.sub: Start with the highlights, or pick a topic.

gef.title: Open GEF and BRO-xml
gef.desc: Cone tests in GEF or BRO-xml, boreholes (BHR-GT, GEF-BORE) and groundwater wells (GMW). Several tests in one file too.

chart.title: qc, fs and Rf by depth
chart.desc: Charts on one depth axis in NAP, with values under the mouse and pore pressure (u2) where measured.

layers.title: Indicative soil layering
layers.desc: Automatic layering on qc and Rf, with minimum thickness and hysteresis. Adjust boundaries yourself and export the layers as JSON with provenance.

normalized.title: Normalized analysis
normalized.desc: Qt, Fr, Bq and Ic per measuring point, with the stresses you enter yourself.

bore.title: Boreholes and groundwater
bore.desc: Borehole logs with layers, colour and admixtures, and groundwater wells with their time series.

validation.title: Data checks
validation.desc: Messages about columns, units, voids and depth, with the line in the source file. Export the check as JSON or CSV.

tabs.title: Several cone tests side by side
tabs.desc: Each file in its own tab, or a project with several tests on one depth axis.

search.title: Search by address
search.desc: Through the PDOK Locatieserver by address, place or RD coordinate.

bro.title: Load BRO data
bro.desc: Cone tests, boreholes and groundwater wells in the visible area, also in large areas above the 2,000-object limit.

pdok.title: PDOK map layers
pdok.desc: Topography, aerial photos of today and of 2016 to 2025, AHN, cadastre, BAG, BGT, zoning plans and historical maps.

measure.title: Measure and export
measure.desc: Measure distances on the map and save the map as an image.

grid.title: Grid of cone tests
grid.desc: Lay out a whole grid of cone tests on the drawing in one go.

edit.title: Drawing tools
edit.desc: Lines, areas, dimension lines and RD coordinates, with move, copy, rotate, trim, extend, mirror and offset.

overlay.title: PDF or image underneath
overlay.desc: A PDF page, photo or SVG frame as background, cropped and to scale.

drawexport.title: PDF on A2 or A3
drawexport.desc: With title block, scale bar and north arrow. The desktop app also exports to DWG.

report.title: PDF report
report.desc: Cover, coordinate table, overview map, a page per cone test, legend and metadata, each on or off.

gefexport.title: Source-faithful GEF export
gefexport.desc: Writes back the original columns, voids and RD/NAP codes, and stops on doubtful source data.

project.title: Own project file
project.desc: Keep cone tests, layers and drawing together in an .ifcgeo file. The desktop app also exports CSV and GeoJSON.

settlement.title: Settlement of one layer
settlement.desc: Concept worksheet in the desktop app, with units and intermediate steps visible.

pad.title: Pad foundation (EC7)
pad.desc: Concept worksheet for a centrally loaded rectangular pad following EC7 Annex D, in the desktop app.

mcp.title: MCP and HTTP API
mcp.desc: An AI assistant or your own script reads cone tests, divides layers and calculates through MCP or a local HTTP API.

core.title: Node library and SDK
core.desc: The same GEF reader, checks and calculations as a separate Node library, plus a native SDK for your own software.

themes.title: Five themes
themes.desc: Light, dark, Blueprint and two high-contrast themes, in the style of all OpenAEC apps.

download.title: Download v2026.44.4

style.title: Five themes
style.desc: New shell and colours in the OpenAEC style 0.4, with light, dark, Blueprint and high contrast.

calc.title: Settlement and pad
calc.desc: Two concept worksheets in the desktop app: settlement of one layer and a pad foundation following EC7.

bro.title: BRO search without gaps
bro.desc: Large areas are split above the 2,000-object limit, and errors are visible.

layers.title: Adjust layers yourself
layers.desc: Minimum thickness, hysteresis and manual layer boundaries, with a JSON export that records provenance.

gef.title: Source-faithful GEF
gef.desc: The GEF export keeps the original columns and is tested against Bedrock and pygef.

signed.title: Signed installers
signed.desc: The downloads for Windows, macOS and Linux are signed and verified before publication.

whatsnew.desc: Four releases came out this week: the style of all OpenAEC apps, signed installers, first calculations in the desktop app and stricter checks of the source data.

files.a: Cone tests in GEF and BRO-xml, boreholes as BHR-GT or GEF-BORE, groundwater wells (GMW) and your own projects in .ifcgeo. You can also open BRO files straight from the map.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: No. The web version works straight in the browser. For the calculations, DWG export and CSV or GeoJSON there is the desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux.

price.q: What does Open Geotechniek Studio cost?
price.a: Nothing. The app is free and open source under the MIT licence, with no account or subscription.

save.q: In which format is my work saved?
save.a: In an .ifcgeo file, an open JSON format with IFCX content. You can also export a cone test back to GEF.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: Windows, macOS (Intel and Apple Silicon) and Linux (.deb and AppImage), and any modern browser. The installers are signed.

practice.a: Yes. It reads GEF and the BRO formats with their quality regimes, describes boreholes following NEN 5104 and works in RD coordinates and NAP. The layering is indicative and does not replace an assessment by a geotechnical engineer.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: The desktop app and the Node library have an MCP server (Model Context Protocol). With it, an assistant such as Claude can read cone tests, fetch BRO data, divide layers, calculate and create a report. There is also a local HTTP API for your own scripts.

internet.q: Do I need an internet connection?
internet.a: Only for the map and the BRO. Your own files are processed on your computer and not uploaded anywhere.

ifc.a: Not yet. An IFC4x3 export is switched off until it meets the schema. The app does already build an experimental IFCX view of your data.

tauri.desc: A thin native shell in Rust for Windows, macOS and Linux, with small, signed installers.

react.desc: The same interface in the browser and on the desktop, with charts drawn on canvas.

core.title: Shared core
core.desc: One GEF reader, check and export for browser, desktop and Node, tested against Bedrock and pygef.

map.desc: Maps in RD and WGS84 with the open map services of the Dutch Kadaster and PDOK.

bro.desc: Cone tests, boreholes and groundwater wells straight from the public Dutch subsurface register.

mcp.title: MCP, HTTP and SDK
mcp.desc: An MCP server, a local HTTP API, a Node library and a native DLL/.so for integrations.
